terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where Idris's stock counts go into your store and come back out.

tasks.title: Keep keys and values
tasks.description:
Implement `open(dir)` and the store's `get(key)` and `set(key, value)` in `src/db.js`.

- `open(dir)` returns a promise of a new store; in this issue the store keeps everything in memory and does not use `dir` yet
- `store.set(key, value)` keeps `value` under `key`; a second `set` of the same key replaces the value
- `store.get(key)` returns the value kept under `key`, exactly as it was given, or `undefined` when the store has no such key
- two stores never share their keys and values

The check opens stores of its own, a fresh one for every case, sets keys and values of its own and reads them back.
nextSteps: Run `node src/try.js` and read the error under the first lines.
In `open`, make somewhere to keep the values, inside that one call.
Return an object with `get` and `set` that reach it.
Run the script again: the counts should come back.
hints: A store is a place for the values and the functions that can reach it. Functions written inside `open` keep the variables of that call for as long as the store exists.
A `Map` keeps values under keys and starts empty: `set` puts a value in, `get` takes it out, and a key it never had gives `undefined`.
In `open`: `const values = new Map()`, then `return { get: (key) => values.get(key), set: (key, value) => { values.set(key, value) } }`.

tasks.title: Tell a missing key from an empty value
tasks.description:
Add `has(key)` and `delete(key)` to the store.

- `store.has(key)` returns `true` when the store holds `key`, even when its value is the empty text `''`, and `false` otherwise
- `get` of a key whose value is `''` gives `''`; `get` of a key that is not there gives `undefined`
- `store.delete(key)` removes the key and its value, so `has` gives `false` and `get` gives `undefined`; other keys stay as they were
- deleting a key that is not there does nothing and does not throw
- a deleted key can be set again

The check sets empty values, deletes keys that are there and keys that are not, and asks `has` and `get` about each.
nextSteps: Read "Missing is not empty" in the lesson.
Write `has` so that it asks whether the key is kept, not what its value is.
Write `delete` so that the key itself goes, not only its value.
Look at the `note` line that `node src/try.js` prints.
hints: An empty text is falsy, so anything that asks `if (value)` treats a note with an empty value as no note at all.
Whether a key is there and what its value is are two questions. A `Map` answers the first with `has`, and removes a key with `delete`.
`has: (key) => values.has(key)` and `delete: (key) => { values.delete(key) }`. Setting the value to `''` or `undefined` is not a delete: the key stays.

tasks.title: Take any text as a key, and only text
tasks.description:
Make the store take every text as a key, and refuse what is not text.

- any text is a key, the empty text `''` included, and so are names that every object already has, like `toString`, `constructor` and `__proto__`: an empty store holds none of them, and each one keeps a value like any other key
- `set(key, value)` throws a `TypeError` when the key or the value is not text, and keeps nothing
- `get`, `has` and `delete` throw a `TypeError` when the key is not text, and leave the store as it was

The check asks a new store about those names, sets values under them, and calls every function with numbers, `null`, `undefined`, objects and arrays.
nextSteps: Read "Any text is a key" in the lesson.
Ask your empty store about `constructor`: does it say no?
Write one small function that throws a `TypeError` for anything that is not text, and call it first in each of the four.
hints: A plain object `{}` is not empty: it already has `toString`, `constructor` and more from `Object.prototype`, and `__proto__` is not an ordinary property on it.
A `Map` starts truly empty and treats every text alike. `typeof key === 'string'` tells you whether a key is text.
`function mustBeText(value) { if (typeof value !== 'string') throw new TypeError('A key or value must be text') }`, called at the top of `get`, `set`, `has` and `delete`, for the value too in `set`.
